originality.rationale: Substantive comparison, not timestamp: Manabe arXiv:2609.05358 gives an explicit sufficient pure-periodicity criterion for {a,b,c} (a>=2 after reduction), least period/P-positions/nim-values only for qualifying non-additive sets, additive c=a+b separate, necessity only conjectured (proved only for period a+b when c>=2(a+b)). It does not record certified (N0,p) cutoffs for the 10 impure sets, maximal-Grundy witnesses M/h, cold counts, or a closed 109-set census with replay certificate. Qin-He arXiv:1208.6134 uses heuristic PTFN to state four empirical period conclusions with no certified (N0,p) proof, no maximal witnesses, no replayable census. Duchene et al. arXiv:1707.07966 proves periodicity transfers to push-the-button compounds of Nim/Wythoff/Euclid and computes no explicit (N0,p)/M table for any concrete subtraction census. Eppstein arXiv:1804.06515 gives O-tilde(n)/O-tilde(mn) algorithms and subtract-a-square experiments, not an explicit cutoff table for primitive 3-sets max<=10. General eventual periodicity is classical existence with exponential bounds and does not mechanically imply exact least (N0,p) or M values. No OEIS finite-3-set entry or textbook table records the paired (N0,p,M,h,nP) census. The paired exact cutoff + maximal-witness table over this closed family is new.

value.rationale: Headline claim is a rigorously established exact invariant of a natural closed object: for every primitive 3-element S with max<=10, the true least eventual SG period p (via Lemma-promoted certificate), least preperiod N0 for that p, and exact windowed maximal nim-value M with least witness h and cold count nP. Object and invariant were motivated before computation (Guy/Berlekamp/Fraenkel periods/preperiods/maximal nim-values; Manabe necessity-conjecture test data; cold-position/sum analysis benchmarks). Values were not known or mechanically implied by general periodicity bounds. A future researcher can reasonably need the precise (N0,p,M,h) fact for a specific set (e.g. longest period 45 at {3,7,10}, largest preperiod 21 at {2,8,9}, binary-valued classification). This is a finite benchmark theorem fragment with seconds-scale replay, not a textbook restatement, parameter substitution, tiny gain, or unexplained enumeration; maximality is windowed and interpreted honestly, and Lemma gives infinite-tail meaning to (N0,p). Census is complete (109/109 closed, no fallback needed), so no incomplete-census discount applies.
